steps: Boil the macaroni in salted water until just tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in the same pot over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for one minute.
Whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheese until smooth.
Fold the macaroni into the sauce, season with salt and pepper and serve hot.
Scramble the eggs with the butter and a pinch of salt until barely set, then let them cool for a few minutes.
Put a spoonful of egg and a handful of cheese in the middle of a wrapper.
Fold in the sides, roll it up tightly and seal the edge with a little water.
Brush the rolls with oil and bake at 220 C (425 F) for 12 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Mash the potatoes and mix in the chili, spices, coriander and salt.
Cut the crusts off the bread and flatten each slice with a rolling pin.
Put some filling on one edge of a slice, wet the other edge and roll it up tightly.
Heat the oil and fry the rolls until golden on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
Crush the cookies, mix with the melted butter and press into the bottom of a lined cake pan.
Spread the chocolate ice cream over the crust and freeze for 30 minutes.
Spread the strawberry ice cream on top, smooth it and drizzle with half of the chocolate syrup.
Freeze for at least 3 hours, until firm.
Top with the sliced strawberries and the rest of the syrup, then slice and serve.
Heat the oven to 220 C (425 F).
Roll the dough into a rectangle and brush it with the garlic butter.
Sprinkle half of the mozzarella over one half of the dough, fold the other half over it and press down.
Cut into strips, twist each one and place on a lined tray.
Top with the rest of the mozzarella, the parmesan and the Italian seasoning.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Peel and grate the potatoes, rinse them in cold water and squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Toss the potatoes with the salt, pepper and cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and press the potatoes into flat patties.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes on each side without moving them, until deep golden and crisp.
Heat the oven to 190 C (375 F) and butter two ramekins, dusting them with the sugar.
Stir the egg yolks into the Nutella until smooth.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gently fold them into the Nutella mixture in two batches.
Fill the ramekins and bake for 14 to 16 minutes without opening the oven door.
Serve right away, before they sink.
Heat half of the cream until it just steams, pour it over the chocolate and stir until smooth, then let it cool.
Whip the rest of the cream to soft peaks.
Fold the whipped cream into the chocolate in two batches until no streaks remain.
Spoon into cups and chill for 2 hours before serving.
Mix the flour, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the green onion and the rest of the salt.
Divide the dough in two and roll each piece into a thin round.
Cook a round on a hot pan with a little butter until spotted, flip it, pour half the egg over it and sprinkle with cheese.
Fold it over, cook until the egg is set and the cheese has melted, then repeat with the second round.
Knead the flour, water and half of the salt into a soft dough and rest it for 15 minutes.
Mix the chicken, cheese, chili, coriander and the rest of the salt for the filling.
Divide the dough into four, roll each piece into a round, add filling in the middle and pinch it closed.
Gently roll each filled ball out again into a flat round.
Cook on a hot pan with a little oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Season the cutlets with salt and pat them dry.
Mix the breadcrumbs, parmesan and Italian seasoning on a plate, beat the eggs in a bowl, and put the flour on another plate.
Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then the parmesan crumbs, pressing the crumbs on.
Fry in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Season the thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear them in the oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes per side until browned.
Stir the honey, soy sauce and garlic together and pour it over the chicken.
Simmer for 5 minutes, spooning the sauce over the thighs, until sticky and cooked through.
Slice each breast open like a book and pound it to an even thickness.
Season both sides with the garlic powder, paprika and salt.
Lay two slices of ham and two of cheese on each breast, roll it up and secure it with toothpicks.
Brown the rolls in the oil, then bake at 200 C (400 F) for 18 to 20 minutes until cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, remove the toothpicks and slice.
Mix half of the yogurt with the lemon juice, garlic, oregano and salt, coat the chicken and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan for 6 to 7 minutes per side until cooked through, then slice it.
Divide the rice between two bowls and top with the chicken, cucumber, tomatoes and feta.
Finish with a spoonful of the remaining yogurt.
Mix the yogurt, garlic powder, paprika, lemon juice, salt and pepper and coat the chicken in it.
Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Place the chicken on a lined tray and bake at 200 C (400 F) for 20 to 25 minutes, until cooked through and no longer pink inside.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Fry the onions in the oil until golden, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste for one minute.
Add the tomatoes, curry powder, turmeric and salt and cook until the tomatoes break down into a thick paste.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the paste.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Pat the wings very dry and toss them with the baking powder, salt and pepper.
Spread them on a rack over a tray and bake at 220 C (425 F) for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Warm the honey, soy sauce, garlic and chili flakes in a small pan for 2 minutes.
Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve at once.
Mix the oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper and lemon juice and rub it all over the drumsticks.
Let them sit for 20 minutes, or longer in the fridge.
Grill over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the juices run clear and the skin is crisp.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Mix the chicken with the egg, garlic paste, chili powder and salt and marinate for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch and flour so each piece has a thin coating.
Heat the oil and fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and crunchy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
Soak the chicken in the buttermilk with half of the salt for at least 30 minutes.
Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and the rest of the salt.
Press each piece of chicken into the flour mixture until thickly coated, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Fry in oil at about 170 C (340 F) for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve hot.
Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili, coriander, cumin and salt for 30 minutes.
Fry the onions in the oil until deep golden, then add the marinated chicken.
Cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring, then lower the heat, cover and cook for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the oil separates.
Stir in the garam masala and serve with rice or flatbread.
